title: Incident healing + customer trust restoration workshop - CardinalPay
summary: Post-incident workshop focused on restoring customer trust after the Oct 5th degradation: review provisional RCA, agree on immediate mitigations (prefix caching rollback, tighter autoscale thresholds), commit to runbook rehearsals and follow-ups (security docs, SOC2 evidence). Agreed next steps: Redwood to send full postmortem + perf logs, schedule runbook drill w/ CardinalPay SREs, provide temporary capacity credit and canary config for dedicated pool. Customer wants audit timeline and evidence of telemetry improved by end of month.
next_steps: Lena to share full postmortem deck and perf logs (link) by 2027-10-15
Schedule runbook/drill with CardinalPay SREs for week of 2027-10-25 (Marcus lead)
Redwood to provide temporary capacity credit + canary config for Dedicated pilot (finance team to confirm)
Sofia to coordinate SOC2 evidence packet and KMS integration notes by 2027-10-22
Aaron to provide list of failing endpoints and sample traces by 2027-10-14
action_items: Lena Park | Share postmortem deck + perf logs | 2027-10-15
Marcus Doyle | Runbook drill plan & runbook updates | 2027-10-20
Sofia Chen | SOC2 docs & KMS integration notes | 2027-10-22
Aaron Li (CardinalPay) | Provide failing endpoint list + traces | 2027-10-14
Rajesh Patel (CardinalPay) | Confirm acceptance criteria for Dedicated pilot | 2027-10-18
transcript:
Header: Date: 2027-10-12, Start: 14:00 UTC, Duration: 58m, Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Rajesh (CTO), Maya (Head of Platform), Tom (Security), Elena (Product), Aaron (SRE)

[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the incident healing workshop, uh, make sure we align on RCA, short term mitigations and a concrete plan to rebuild trust. appreciate folks making time.
[00:18] Rajesh (CardinalPay): Thanks, yeah. appreciate you pulling this together. big thing for us is timeline — customers saw payment verification timeouts and a chunk of auth traffic dropped last week. we lost 7.2% of conversions during the window so it's pretty visible.
[00:35] Marcus (Redwood SE): Right — quick recap: on Oct 5th we saw a surge in long sequence generation requests hitting a lived-in model variant. automatic batching spiked, KV cache grew large and we hit a pathological memory footprint on the pod, which triggered backoff and evictions. the autoscaler responded but oscillated because the health probe latencies crossed the threshold repeatedly.
[00:58] Aaron (CardinalPay SRE): to add — we had an upstream retry loop on our side that amplified the load. some of our clients retried aggressively for tokens that were actually still being processed, so we got thundering-herd-like behavior.
[01:11] Maya (Head of Platform): also, our edge timeout was 3s, but the service sometimes took 6-8s under pressure. so clients retried. full feedback loop.
[01:22] Tom (Security): real quick — any data exfil concerns? we had compliance pinging us, they want to see logs and KMS usage during the window.
[01:30] Lena: totally. Sofia will lead that and we'll share a SOC2-adjacent evidence packet and the KMS key rotation logs. Marcus, do you want to walk through the provisional RCA we posted? link — https://redwood.example.com/postmortem/cardinalpay-2027-10-05 (note: internal link).
[01:48] Marcus: yeah I'll share screen (audio only) — so slide 3 shows timeline. the root cause we think is a combination: 1) a workload pattern change (longer prompts from a new product flow) 2) autoscale thresholds tuned for steady throughput which didn't handle rapid spike, 3) a prefix/KV cache policy that allowed unbounded growth for that tenant due to a cache key bug — transcription sometimes shows it as KV cash in the logs, ha — but it's KV cache.
[02:14] Rajesh: can you clarify the cache key bug? is it leaking keys across sessions?
[02:20] Marcus: good q. it's not cross-tenant, but a cache eviction policy mis-eval: we were incorrectly computing TTLs when the user prompt contained special chars — which caused the cache to mark entries as sticky. so we effectively had a cache growth for certain requests.
[02:40] Elena (Product): that special char flow is coming from our new doc upload feature. we rolled it last week.
[02:46] Lena: ok so product change + tuned infra = perfect storm.
[02:52] Rajesh: what's the immediate mitigation we should accept? we rolled back the prefix cache at 02:10 on Oct 6 and it helped, but we still had issues later in the day.
[03:03] Marcus: immediate mitigation stack we recommend: 1) rollback the sticky key change (already done on Oct 6), 2) enforce a hard cap on KV cache size per-tenant, 3) tighten autoscale hysteresis and increase probe window to avoid oscillation, 4) add short-term per-route rate limiting and retry suppression at the edge for that product path.
[03:24] Aaron: the edge rate limit would be the cleanest short-term step. we can push that internally within a day.
[03:29] Maya: we need to be careful about breaking UX. what about a canary first?
[03:33] Marcus: yes canary is key — Redwood can provide a canary config for Dedicated or Hosted route. we'll propose a canary with a reduced QPS and tighter per-request token limit.
[03:44] Tom: and from security — we need to see the perf logs, request traces and evidence that no PII left traces in the cache. is that plausible to produce?
[03:53] Sofia (CSM): yes, we'll provide redacted traces and a cache snapshot. note that the KV cache is encrypted at rest via KMS but we will extract logs to show no PII — details in SOC packet.
[04:04] Rajesh: timeline? our compliance team wants something by Oct 22.
[04:09] Sofia: we can aim for Oct 22 for the evidence packet. Lena will send the postmortem deck sooner — by Oct 15 — with perf logs and a short one-page incident brief for exec comms.
[04:22] Lena: agreed. now about trust restoration and commercial remediation — Marcus, do you want to run the safety nets we can provide?
[04:29] Marcus: sure — options: 1) temporary capacity credit applied to next invoice, 2) a short Dedicated pilot (isolated pool) with canary config to prove steady latency under load, 3) weekly runbook drills for the next 6 weeks with joint Redwood/CardinalPay SREs, 4) extended telemetry retention for deeper root cause checks.
[04:50] Rajesh: the Dedicated pilot is attractive if it's limited and we can validate latency. credits are fine too but we care more about preventing recurrence.
[04:58] Lena: we can offer a 30-day Dedicated pilot with a reserved pool and a SLO for p95 under 1200ms for the product route; finance will confirm credit details.
[05:09] Elena: we'll need to include product owners in the pilot acceptance criteria — I propose a simple checklist: no more than 1% error rate, p95 < 1200ms for 7 of 10 days, and no cache overgrowth events.
[05:24] Marcus: sounds reasonable. we'll instrument synthetic traffic and provide dashboards in Redwood Console for transparency.
[05:32] Rajesh: good. one thing — during the incident we saw the autoscaler create pods with incompatible kernel settings causing degraded perf in 3 of 12 pods. is that fixed?
[05:43] Marcus: yes — we applied a kernel-constrained image in the patch on Oct 7. that image pins scheduler parameters and has improved warm-start times. but we should validate under CardinalPay load patterns.
[05:55] Aaron: can we get a post-deploy validation checklist? we had pods come up but readiness probes were flapping.
[06:02] Marcus: we'll share a checklist for readiness gating — and include sanity checks for memory footprint and KV cache depth.
[06:10] Tom: another compliance ask — show that key rotations happened and that KMS access was normal. also need audit logs for admin access during the window.
[06:20] Sofia: we'll include admin audit logs and KMS access logs in the packet. note that some entries may be redacted for internal ops accounts.
[06:28] Rajesh: on communication — we want an external postmortem draft for customers that we can co-sign. can Redwood provide a template?
[06:35] Lena: yes, we'll draft a customer-facing one-page summary and share for approval. Marcus will provide the technical appendix.
[06:42] Elena: timeline for that? our comms team is ready to send by Oct 18 if we have the draft by Oct 15.
[06:50] Lena: ok — postmortem draft to CardinalPay by Oct 15.
[06:55] Rajesh: I appreciate that. next, runbook rehearsal — how often do you recommend?
[07:01] Marcus: weekly for first 3 weeks, then bi-weekly for next month. each session 60m — one injected failure scenario and a live mitigation. we'll use canary traffic and a replay harness.
[07:14] Aaron: count us in. we want to test the edge rate limit + backoff suppression.
[07:20] Marcus: perfect; Marcus will own the plan and Lena will book the sessions.
[07:25] Tom: security note — make sure runbook access is RBAC-limited; our auditors will want proof of separation of duties.
[07:32] Sofia: we'll restrict runbook editor role to Redwood SEs and CardinalPay SREs.
[07:36] Rajesh: on the commercial side, I want to ensure this doesn't hit our SLA credits process incorrectly. we'll need a statement of work for any Dedicated pilot.
[07:45] Lena: finance will prepare SOW & pilot terms; I'll loop you in.
[07:49] Elena: small UX ask — can we get a short list of recommended prompt length limits that reduce KV cache pressure without changing product behavior too much?
[07:58] Marcus: yes — we'll provide guidance and suggested token limits per route; we can also offer client-side truncation libraries.
[08:06] Rajesh: any longer-term fixes? we're concerned about unpredictable model variants causing resource spikes.
[08:11] Marcus: long-term we're proposing model traffic shaping: 1) route heavy generation to a Dedicated pool optimized for long sequences, 2) provide model quantization profiles to reduce memory, 3) persistent per-tenant cache quotas with eviction backpressure to the app layer.
[08:28] Maya: great. what about monitoring — we need alert fidelity improvements. we were getting alerts but they weren't actionable.
[08:34] Marcus: we'll add SLO-based alerts and a composite alert that maps to candidate causes (cache growth, pod OOM, autoscale thrash). also add a playbook link in the alert.
[08:45] Aaron: sample traces — I'll upload a set of traces and failing requests to the shared folder after the call.
[08:52] Lena: perfect — include the span IDs.
[08:55] Rajesh: last question — do you think NimbusAI or CloudServe have better guardrails for this pattern? not to be rude but we evaluate options.
[09:03] Lena: competitors have some different autoscale heuristics but they also trade off latency predictability. we think Dedicated + canary + strict cache quotas is the right approach. Marcus, maybe note competitor differences in the appendix.
[09:15] Marcus: will do; short note: some competitors avoid KV cache and rely on prefix pruning, which reduces memory but increases token cost. it's a tradeoff.
[09:26] Sofia: ok wrapping up — quick recap of agreed items: postmortem deck by Oct 15, runbook drill schedule week of Oct 25, SOC2 evidence by Oct 22, Dedicated pilot proposal and SOW to follow.
[09:42] Rajesh: thanks all. we need to restore confidence quickly. appreciate the pragmatic remediation plan.
[09:48] Lena: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the links and action items.
[09:52] (crosstalk) Marcus: thanks. bye.

Notes: occasional transcription errors (KV "cash"), speaker labels sometimes simplified. Shared artifacts: postmortem draft link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/postmortem/cardinalpay-2027-10-05 , canary config draft: https://redwood.example.com/canaries/cardinalpay-dedicated-proposal , shared folder for traces: https://redwood.example.com/share/cardinalpay-traces-10-12

End of transcript.
